policydecision_details: Launched the 2026 date harvest season in Jericho and the Jordan Valley, highlighting the importance of the date sector to agricultural production, employment, and exports. Official estimates put this season’s production at around 28,860 tonnes, from approximately 361,000 palm trees across more than 889 farms. The ministry is strengthening data collection, production estimates, coordination, and sector governance to improve planning, marketing, and export competitiveness, while supporting farmers and the continued development of the date value chain. The previous season recorded around 17,000 tonnes of exports, valued at more than NIS400 million.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Launched an awareness campaign to encourage farmers to join organized agricultural production groups. The initiative aims to strengthen collective action, improve production volume and quality, reduce input and service costs, and facilitate access to agricultural extension, training, inputs, and marketing opportunities. Producer groups will also help farmers coordinate production and marketing, exchange knowledge and services, improve crop quality and productivity, and strengthen links with local markets and agro-processing industries.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

policydecision_details: Launched the STAR programme, a six-year initiative supported by USD 175 million from the World Bank to increase agricultural production and strengthen the participation of cooperatives and the private sector. The programme will rehabilitate seed cleaning and treatment centres and storage facilities, provide improved drought-resistant varieties, and support farmers in adopting better agricultural practices and organic certification to strengthen export opportunities. It will also target the drought-affected governorates of Hasaka, Raqqa and Deir Ezzor, which are important for wheat, barley and livestock production.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Launched a project worth approximately NIS3.5 million to strengthen climate adaptation and sustainable agriculture through integrated water-resource development in the eastern slopes. The 2026–2028 project will rehabilitate water-harvesting facilities, wells and springs, improve irrigation efficiency, develop around 200 dunums of irrigated agricultural land, and provide water tanks to farming households. It will also train around 510 farmers in sustainable water management and climate-smart agriculture, strengthen institutional capacity, and develop a digital agricultural and water database to support planning and decision-making.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Distributed irrigation conveyance lines and irrigation networks, including valves and connection heads, to 77 farmers in the Dhuhaibat Al-Dahdouh area of Gaza. The intervention responds to extensive damage to agricultural land, infrastructure, equipment, and irrigation systems caused by the war, helping farmers restore basic production capacity and resume cultivation on available land. The project is part of broader agricultural recovery efforts to support farmers’ resilience, sustain production, and contribute to the gradual restoration of the agricultural sector in Gaza.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Began distributing biological control agents, including aphid lions, to citrus orchards in different areas of Tartous Governorate. The initiative supports integrated pest management by strengthening the use of natural enemies to control pests, reduce reliance on chemical pesticides, and maintain ecological balance in orchards. The programme also aims to improve the safety and quality of citrus products by reducing pesticide residues, with distribution planned in phases according to pest infestation levels and orchard needs.
decision_making_institution: Citrus Office – Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Introduced a new import licensing system for fresh garlic (HS 07032000) entering the Moroccan market. The measure is expected to regulate garlic imports and support domestic production, while Spanish garlic exporters and the National Association of Garlic Growers and Traders of Spain (ANPCA) raised concerns that the new licensing requirements could complicate trade with Morocco, an important market for Spanish garlic. The development highlights Morocco’s use of trade policy instruments to manage agricultural imports and protect domestic producers.
decision_making_institution: Government of Morocco
commodity1: Other products, not included in the other categories

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Launched the “Green Legacy, Lasting Planting” greening project to expand green spaces and improve vegetation across its wilayats through participation from government entities, the private sector, civil society and local communities. The initiative aims to make tree planting part of longer-term sustainable development, supporting climate adaptation, resource efficiency, carbon reduction and improved urban environments. It also seeks to generate social, economic and tourism benefits by enhancing public spaces and supporting activities linked to agriculture and planting.
decision_making_institution: The Office of the Governor of Al Sharqiyah North Governorate
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Approved new regulations governing the sale, purchase, rental, and exchange of camels across Saudi Arabia. The regulations establish an integrated framework for documenting ownership and transactions, strengthening health, biosecurity, vaccination, transportation, and registration requirements, while improving animal welfare in markets, exhibitions, and auctions. The rules also require electronic documentation of contracts and ownership transfers and introduce penalties for violations, supporting more transparent and regulated camel trading and livestock management.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The FAO and the National Agricultural Research Centre (NARC) signed an agreement to strengthen drought adaptation and climate resilience in Jordan’s agricultural sector, with support from the Government of Japan. The project will support drought-affected farming communities through training and field demonstrations on climate-resilient agriculture, sustainable beekeeping, permaculture, composting, regenerative soil management, and improved land and water management. It will also strengthen institutional capacity, establish a demonstration and training site, and promote innovative, nature-inclusive agricultural practices to restore livelihoods, improve natural resource management, and support sustainable agricultural production and food security.
decision_making_institution: The National Agricultural Research Centre (NARC)
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Launched an agricultural project in Dodoma, to plant 3,000 date palm seedlings and strengthen farmers’ resilience to drought. The initiative includes pilot fields, irrigation systems, agricultural machinery, and training for farmers and extension staff, directly supporting 250 smallholder farmers and indirectly benefiting around 1,150 people. The project aims to diversify rural incomes, promote sustainable agricultural practices, and strengthen food security.
decision_making_institution: King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief)

policydecision_details: Launched a 2026–2030 national programme to rebuild livestock production after years of drought, declining forage resources and rising production costs. The programme, backed by around TND 93 million in direct government funding, aims to increase milk production by 11% to about 1.4 million tonnes, raise red meat production by 17% to around 281,000 tonnes, and rebuild the cattle herd through improved breeding, farmer support and modern production practices. Measures also include expanding local forage and pastoral resources, strengthening veterinary services, improving livestock identification and traceability, and providing direct financial support to farmers for improved breeding animals and the retention of young female livestock.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture (Office of Livestock and Pastures)

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation and the American University in Cairo (AUC) signed an agreement to implement the Building Climate Leadership Excellence for African Resilience (BCLEAR) programme, aimed at strengthening the capacity of African water professionals. The programme will deliver four training-of-trainers programmes in Egypt, Uganda and Rwanda, covering climate-smart agriculture, sustainable water management, crop and water management, integrated resource planning, and the water-energy-food-ecosystems (WEFE) nexus. It will establish a network of African trainers and specialists who can transfer knowledge to national institutions, strengthen institutional capacity, and promote knowledge exchange and cooperation, particularly among Nile Basin countries.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation

policydecision_details: Processed and issued approvals and completion certificates for refrigerated and frozen storage facilities across Iraq, with total storage capacity reaching 241,298 tonnes refrigerated and 172,543 tonnes frozen. The measures included establishing and renewing licences, technical and field inspections, and completion certificates for storage projects in Baghdad and Nineveh. The initiative aims to strengthen agricultural storage infrastructure, reduce post-harvest losses, improve the handling and marketing of agricultural products, support investment in the agricultural sector, and contribute to food security.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Carried out rehabilitation and maintenance works on forest roads in the Jisr al-Shughur area after more than 14 years without maintenance. The works included removing soil, vegetation and other obstacles from road routes to improve access for forestry patrols, firefighting teams and vehicles, particularly during the fire season. The initiative aims to strengthen forest protection, improve emergency preparedness and facilitate access to forested areas.
decision_making_institution: Land Reclamation Directorate

policy_description: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
policydecision_details: Announced the closure of the shrimp fishing season in Yemen’s Red Sea waters to protect shrimp stocks and prevent overfishing. The ministry instructed the General Authority for Red Sea Fisheries to inventory shrimp stocks held in cold storage and the General Authority for Marine Science and Research to conduct an urgent study on shrimp breeding seasons to inform future fishing seasons. Fisheries authorities and the Coast Guard will also strengthen maritime monitoring and enforcement during the closure to support the sustainable management and protection of marine resources.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources
policycategory: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations

policydecision_details: Distributed locally produced seeders and grain sieves to agricultural cooperative associations across the governorate. The initiative aims to strengthen farmers’ capacity, support agricultural value chains, facilitate maize harvesting, reduce dependence on imports and contribute to greater agricultural self-sufficiency.
decision_making_institution: Unit for Financing Agricultural and Fisheries Projects and Initiatives – Al-Dhale' Governorate

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Signed a €3.3 million consultancy agreement to support a project improving energy efficiency through biogas power generation at wastewater treatment plants. Supported by German cooperation and EU co-financing, the project will rehabilitate wastewater treatment facilities, develop sludge treatment and biogas production systems, generate electricity on site, and improve treated wastewater quality for safe agricultural reuse. The initiative aims to strengthen water and resource management, reduce greenhouse gas emissions and operating costs, increase clean energy use, and support Jordan’s water security and sustainable development.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Water and Irrigation
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Launched the second phase of an awareness programme on rooftop rainwater harvesting and efficient water use in Karak, Tafileh and Maan. Funded by the Green Climate Fund (GCF), the initiative targets students, government employees and local communities and will support the installation of rainwater harvesting systems in 75 public schools and 150 public buildings. The programme promotes water conservation, household water-saving measures and climate change adaptation, supporting more sustainable use of Jordan’s limited water resources and improving the resilience of communities and the agricultural sector.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Water and Irrigation / Ministry of Agriculture / Ministry of Environment

policydecision_details: Jordan and the Russian Federation agreed on measures to strengthen bilateral trade, investment and economic cooperation across key sectors, including agriculture, food security, energy, transport, logistics and manufacturing. The two sides discussed removing trade barriers, improving market access, expanding private-sector investment and strengthening regulatory and data-sharing cooperation, including with the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU). The initiative aims to diversify Jordan’s trade opportunities and expand exports and investment links with Russia and EAEU markets.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Industry, Trade and Supply

policydecision_details: Launched eight integrated international logistics corridors connecting seaports on the Red Sea and Mediterranean with the Suez Canal, dry ports, and industrial, agricultural, and mining zones. The corridors use railways, electric high-speed rail, and highways to improve connectivity with markets in the Gulf, Levant, Africa, Europe, and Asia, while reducing cargo handling times and logistics costs. The wider maritime transport plan also includes expanding commercial ports, berths, and supporting infrastructure, strengthening Egypt’s role as a regional logistics and trade hub and improving the movement of agricultural and other goods.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Transport

policydecision_details: The dairy goat distribution project in Dongola aims to support livelihoods and economic recovery by providing dairy goats to vulnerable families across North Nile State. The project is expected to benefit around 1,500 families, including 400 families in Dongola through the distribution of 1,200 dairy goats, alongside training on animal management and production. The initiative seeks to strengthen household income, livestock production, and community resilience, with additional productive projects planned in fisheries and other sectors.
decision_making_institution: North Nile State Secretariat for Social Affairs

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Strenghtened its climate-finance framework to expand the pipeline of bankable, investment-ready green projects, particularly in renewable energy and green hydrogen. The Green Climate Fund approved a 36-month readiness programme to support a Climate Investment Plan and Financing Framework, improve project-pipeline management, strengthen climate-finance tracking, and develop investment proposals. The initiative highlights the importance of blended finance, project preparation, consistent green-taxonomy standards, and reliable climate-risk data to mobilize international investment and support Oman’s transition to a resilient, low-carbon economy.
decision_making_institution: Government of Oman / Green Climate Fund (GCF)
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Introduced a temporary 15% import tariff on selected vegetables during periods when locally produced supplies are available, under Decree No. 45 of 2026. The tariff applies to imported fresh or chilled tomatoes from January to May, eggplants from January to April and November to December, and zucchini from January to April and October to December. Outside these periods, standard customs rates apply. The measure is intended to adjust import conditions in line with seasonal domestic production while giving importers time to adapt their supply and pricing arrangements.
decision_making_institution: Government of Qatar

policydecision_details: Introduced and adapted promising pistachio varieties with demonstrated tolerance to drought and high temperatures under the national programme for propagating fruit and olive varieties. The trials have reached the fruiting and harvesting stage, allowing researchers to assess the suitability of these varieties to local climatic conditions and identify those suitable for expanding pistachio cultivation in appropriate areas.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Implemented an integrated agricultural intervention in Um Al-Batoum valued at approximately NIS62,000, benefiting 26 residents. The project provided 9.5 tonnes of animal feed, agricultural land fencing, home gardens with vegetable seedlings and organic fertilizers, and rehabilitation of three water wells to support livestock, household production, and access to water for agricultural activities. Implemented under the “Sumoud” project for food sovereignty in besieged villages, the intervention aims to strengthen food security, livelihoods, and the ability of vulnerable agricultural communities to continue production and remain on their land.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Carried out a campaign to maintain and rehabilitate pesticide sprayers and other equipment used in agricultural pest-control operations. The work aims to maintain agricultural equipment, ensure operational efficiency, protect public assets, and support the effective implementation of pest-control campaigns. Technical recommendations were also provided to agricultural staff on the proper use and maintenance of the equipment to extend its operational life.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Strenghtened an integrated national production ecosystem linking agriculture, food production, manufacturing, quality standards, technology, supply chains, and international markets. Key measures include the National Project for UAE Good Agricultural Practices (UAE GAP), which aims to improve local production standards and market access, the National Agriculture Initiative for Climate-Smart Crops to diversify the food basket and reduce import dependence, and the Sustainable Product initiative to increase the use of locally produced agricultural and livestock products in the hospitality sector. Other initiatives support geographically defined products, industrial resilience, local procurement, technology adoption, recycling, and factory modernization, helping strengthen domestic value addition, supply-chain resilience, and the competitiveness of UAE products in regional and global markets.
decision_making_institution: The Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

policydecision_details: Signed 40 agreements to rehabilitate and maintain traditional aflaj irrigation systems and drill auxiliary wells across A’Dhahirah Governorate, with a total value of approximately OMR621,363. The programme includes 35 agreements for the maintenance and rehabilitation of damaged aflaj and five agreements for auxiliary wells and related facilities. The projects aim to restore water flows, improve the reliability and sustainability of irrigation supplies, and support agricultural land and water-resource management in the governorate.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

policydecision_details: Signed five agreements and memorandums of understanding with private-sector partners to expand investment, research, innovation, and sustainable development across Saudi Arabia’s agricultural and environmental sectors. The partnerships cover agricultural research and development, poultry production, environmental investment, financing, technology localization, sustainability initiatives, and capacity building. They also include support for the Al-Ahsa Green initiative and mangrove restoration in the Red Sea, while promoting knowledge exchange and greater private-sector participation in achieving the objectives of Saudi Vision 2030 and the National Environment Strategy.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

policydecision_details: Promoted innovative irrigation solutions to improve water-use efficiency and expand the use of treated water in landscaping and urban greening. The Irrigation Solutions Innovation Competition, launched under the Tree Week Initiative, evaluates practical irrigation technologies from technical, operational, economic, and scalability perspectives. The initiative supports more efficient irrigation networks, expansion of green spaces, and the national afforestation plan to double the number of trees by 2035, contributing to Bahrain’s environmental sustainability and climate action objectives.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Municipalities and Agriculture

policy_description: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
policydecision_details: Introduced updated conditions and procedures for bluefin tuna fishing by nationally flagged vessels, strengthening the regulatory and monitoring framework for the sector. The decree clarifies rules for live tuna transfers, defines support vessels and tuna fattening operations, and introduces control tools such as the electronic Bluefin Catch Document (eBCD) and stereoscopic cameras to improve the measurement and recording of catches. It also strengthens oversight of fish killing, transfers, feeding and the use of control cages to improve traceability, monitoring, and compliance with bluefin tuna management requirements.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development
policycategory: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations

policydecision_details: Supported rural women through productive agricultural and livestock projects that generate sustainable household income and contribute to food security. Around 90 rural women are registered in productive projects, covering activities such as food processing, goat, sheep and poultry production, beekeeping, and home farming. The Directorate provides technical support through field follow-up and training in project management, packaging, and digital and traditional marketing, while facilitating access to financing and opportunities to participate in exhibitions, festivals, and permanent sales outlets. The initiative aims to strengthen women’s economic participation, improve the sustainability of rural enterprises, and increase the marketability of locally produced goods.
decision_making_institution: The Directorate General of Agriculture and Water Resources

policydecision_details: Promoted investment in mango production to reduce reliance on imports, increase domestic production, and strengthen the crop’s economic value chain. The country currently imports around 46,211 tonnes of mangoes annually, valued at approximately OMR18.7 million, while domestic production exceeded 17,123 tonnes in 2025. The 2026–2030 localization plan aims to expand cultivated area to around 10,300 feddans and increase production to nearly 44,785 tonnes, supported by improved productivity, water-use efficiency, modern irrigation, better varieties, and agricultural research. The initiative also seeks to develop activities across the value chain, including nurseries, packaging, storage, logistics, processing, and marketing, creating opportunities for private investment, SMEs, employment, and food security.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

policydecision_details: Launched a Green Artificial Intelligence Alliance to promote the use of renewable and low-emission energy in artificial intelligence and high-performance computing. The initiative brings together government entities, private-sector companies, academic and research institutions, and investors to develop a national ecosystem for sustainable AI. Its 2026 work plan includes supporting research on energy-efficient computing, building national expertise, encouraging private-sector adoption of green technologies, and developing incentives for investment in clean digital solutions. The alliance supports Oman Vision 2040 by linking digital transformation and AI development with environmental sustainability, renewable energy, and economic development.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture and the Palestinian Standards and Metrology Institution signed a technical cooperation agreement to implement a training and capacity-building programme on the Palestinian Good Agricultural Practices system (PAL-GAP – PS 4109). The programme will train 50 agricultural engineers from the Ministry as assistant advisors in applying good agricultural practices, with theoretical and practical training covering quality standards, certification requirements, and field implementation. Funded by the World Bank under the Social Recovery and Job Creation in Agriculture project, the initiative aims to improve the quality and competitiveness of Palestinian agricultural products, strengthen food safety and standards, and support access to export markets, particularly for products such as dates and olive oil.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Launched a pilot electronic system for managing employee leave and personnel movements as part of its digital transformation efforts. Developed by the Ministry’s Electronic Computing Department, the system digitises leave requests, study leave, ministry orders, training courses, official movement permits, and other administrative procedures, reducing paper-based transactions and improving data management and monitoring. The pilot phase will assess the system’s efficiency, identify and address issues, and support a potential rollout across other Ministry departments and units.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Approved an amendment allowing crude oil exports to Türkiye of up to 33,000 barrels per day as an initial stage, linked to the financing mechanism of the bilateral water framework agreement between the two countries. The decision connects Iraq’s oil export revenues with the financing of water-related cooperation and infrastructure under the agreement.
decision_making_institution: Government of Iraq

policydecision_details: Supplied two electronic milking systems to model sheep farms in Yatta, Hebron, and Masafer Bani Na'im, at a total cost of approximately NIS 945,000 under the Sustainable Livestock Development Programme. The systems will support small-ruminant breed improvement by providing accurate milk-production data, updating farm records electronically, and improving herd and feeding management. The initiative aims to increase livestock productivity, reduce the time, effort, and costs associated with milking, support genetic selection and breeding programmes, improve the quality of animal products, and strengthen farmers’ resilience and sustainable livestock production.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Signed an agreement to construct an integrated fishing port in Mahout, Al Wusta Governorate, to strengthen the fisheries sector and support investment and local economic development. The project will improve fish landing, handling, marketing, storage, and processing facilities, while providing services for fishermen and creating opportunities for fish-processing industries, tourism, and maritime activities. The port will include breakwaters, berths, floating pontoons, a fish market, ice plants, vessel repair workshops, fishermen’s facilities, fish-processing plots, and supporting electricity, water, sewage, and road infrastructure. Given Mahout’s major role in the governorate’s fishing activity, the project is expected to increase the added value of fisheries products, support local communities, and contribute to the diversification and sustainable development of Oman’s fisheries economy.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation (Egypt) and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) signed cooperation agreements to develop a master plan for agricultural and rural development in South Sinai and establish a strategic framework for Egypt’s olive value chain. The South Sinai initiative will focus on empowering local communities, particularly youth and women, creating sustainable livelihoods, improving the use of natural resources, and integrating local production into agricultural and food value chains. The olive-sector framework will assess the value chain from production and processing to marketing and consumption, identifying opportunities to increase productivity and competitiveness and inform a national strategy for sustainable growth and food security.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture and FAO signed 13 investment support agreements under the 18th round of the MAP II programme, supporting market-oriented agricultural investments, innovation, and the development of a sustainable food system across six Palestinian governorates. The projects represent a total investment of approximately NIS 4.35 million, with NIS 2.03 million provided by the programme and NIS 2.32 million contributed by beneficiaries. Supported activities include crop and livestock production, grain and animal feed production, food processing, packaging, and energy and water projects, selected based on their productivity, quality, and sustainability. The programme also supports Palestinian farmers and agricultural production amid the destruction and targeting of land, people, and water, contributing to food and water security and farmers’ resilience.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Launched a programme to install solar photovoltaic systems at public buildings operated by municipalities, expanding the use of renewable energy and improving energy efficiency across the Kingdom. The programme targets 104 municipalities and 188 municipal buildings, with a combined capacity of up to 3.4 MW, expected to reduce municipal electricity costs by around JD550,000 annually and cut carbon emissions by approximately 3,838 tonnes per year. It also includes specialised training for more than 550 municipal employees to strengthen local capacity for the operation and maintenance of the systems and ensure their long-term sustainability. The initiative supports Jordan’s energy transition, reduces the financial burden on municipalities, and promotes more sustainable local public services.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Launched a SAR 3.5 million project to improve urban water systems in Taiz, in partnership with Selah Foundation for Development. The project will strengthen the institutional and technical capacity of the local water and sanitation corporation, improve asset management and operation and maintenance, and reduce water losses. Together with a complementary French-funded project, the initiatives total SAR 7.4 million and are expected to directly benefit more than 139,000 people and indirectly benefit over 242,000, while improving the resilience of urban water infrastructure to climate-change impacts. The project forms part of SDRPY’s wider water-sector and development support across Yemen.
decision_making_institution: Saudi Development and Reconstruction Program for Yemen (SDRPY)

policydecision_details: Qatar and Guyana signed a memorandum of understanding to strengthen cooperation in agriculture and technology, covering crops, livestock, and fisheries. The agreement provides for the exchange of expertise, training, capacity building, and modern agricultural technologies, with the aim of supporting sustainable agricultural development and improving food security and supply chains. It also seeks to diversify food supply sources and create new opportunities for investment and cooperation between the two countries.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Municipality

policydecision_details: Iraq and Brazil agreed to proceed with signing memoranda of understanding (MoUs) covering livestock and crop production, following discussions on expanding agricultural cooperation. The talks focused particularly on developing Iraq’s poultry sector and strengthening broader cooperation in agricultural production. The agreement is expected to provide a framework for closer technical and sectoral collaboration between the two countries.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Supplied the sheep farm at Beit Qad Agricultural Research Station in Jenin with modern equipment and technologies worth approximately NIS 822,150 under the Sustainable Livestock Development Programme. The equipment includes electronic animal identification and herd data-management systems, feeding and livestock-production equipment, and specialized technologies to support genetic improvement and the production and preservation of improved genetic material. The initiative aims to improve herd management, milking and production efficiency, strengthen the station’s research and genetic improvement capacity, and support livestock productivity, food security, and the resilience of farmers and livestock breeders.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Signed a memorandum of understanding with Nutanix to explore the modernization of the Ministry’s digital infrastructure through hybrid multicloud technologies and artificial intelligence. The cooperation aims to strengthen business continuity, disaster recovery, cybersecurity, and the secure management of applications and data across different cloud environments. It also includes knowledge transfer and development of national technical skills, supporting the localization of advanced technology and MEWA’s broader digital transformation efforts.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

policydecision_details: Began compensating farmers and livestock breeders affected by recent agricultural fires triggered by El Niño, starting in Jijel with the distribution of livestock to affected breeders. The compensation programme will extend to all affected provinces and aims to restore agricultural activity as quickly as possible. Support includes the distribution of cattle, sheep, goats, and fodder, while specialized agricultural companies are rehabilitating damaged production infrastructure such as stables and poultry houses. Compensation will cover losses identified by local assessment committees, including livestock, production facilities, irrigation networks, beehives, and poultry houses, helping affected producers resume agricultural activities and rebuild their livelihoods.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Fisheries

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Agriculture and Ministry of Labour, through the Palestinian Employment Fund, signed agricultural grant agreements for 9 beneficiaries under the second phase of the SANIT project – Supporting the Agricultural and Food Cooperation Network in Palestine, with total grants of NIS 235,000. The grants target the fodder and plum sectors and aim to support sustainable agricultural businesses, strengthen agricultural value chains, create employment opportunities, increase production, and improve food security. Beneficiaries were selected through a competitive technical process based on project feasibility, sustainability, environmental impact, job creation, innovation, market access, and cooperative participation. The initiative also provides beneficiaries with agricultural extension and technical support to improve the productivity and long-term sustainability of their projects.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Ministry of Labour

policydecision_details: Launched the “Buthra” (Seed) initiative, a project aimed at economically empowering rural women and strengthening their role in agricultural and rural development. The initiative targets 520 vulnerable women through vocational training, support for small productive projects, and improved access to markets for rural products, helping increase income opportunities, improve livelihoods, and strengthen food security. The project also supports the development of sustainable rural enterprises and creates a more enabling environment for women to turn their productive skills into sustainable economic opportunities.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Launched the rehabilitation and development of the Al-Jalaa date palm farm in the Al-Bukamal area, in partnership with the Relief American Fund. The project covers approximately 2,000 dunums and around 12,000 date palms across 25 varieties, with planned improvements including fertilization and pest control, irrigation and infrastructure rehabilitation, solar energy, planting new offshoots, and agricultural training and knowledge transfer. The project also includes developing facilities for agritourism and related services, helping increase the farm’s economic value and support the development of the date palm sector in the area.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Launched the National Livestock Vaccination Project for the 2026/2027 season in North Al Batinah Governorate, targeting more than 500,000 livestock through six veterinary clinics and two mobile veterinary clinics. The programme aims to strengthen animal health, prevent livestock diseases, improve veterinary services, and support sustainable animal production and food security. Building on the previous season, when more than 900,000 vaccine doses were administered to over 449,000 livestock, the new programme will expand vaccination coverage to more than 70% of the governorate’s livestock population. A new digital vaccination platform will also improve field monitoring, data management, performance tracking, and decision-making.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

policydecision_details: Directed the implementation of a Cairo greening project to transform spaces cleared through urban redevelopment into green areas, alongside the restoration of historic and Islamic Cairo and the upgrading of infrastructure around heritage sites. The initiative aims to increase urban greenery, improve the capital’s environment, and enhance the use and attractiveness of historic areas through integrated heritage and tourism development. The government targets increasing the per-capita share of urban green space to 3 square metres by 2030, while the project is also linked to broader efforts to restore Cairo’s historic landmarks and improve the use of public and heritage spaces.
decision_making_institution: Government of Egypt

policydecision_details: Launched the Water Regulation Forum as an international platform to strengthen cooperation among water-sector regulators and promote more adaptive, efficient, and sustainable regulatory frameworks. The forum will bring together regulators, policymakers, financial and international institutions, and water-sector experts to address challenges such as water scarcity, climate change, desalination, water reuse, investment, and digital transformation. Drawing on Saudi Arabia’s experience in managing one of the world’s largest integrated water systems, the initiative will facilitate knowledge exchange, compare regulatory approaches, and develop practices that can improve water-sector resilience, efficiency, service quality, and investment. The forum will also establish the Water Regulation Exchange (WREx) as a future annual platform for international regulatory cooperation and knowledge sharing.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Three UAE-backed solar power plants were inaugurated in Comoros, with a combined capacity of approximately 20 MW, supported by battery storage and new transmission infrastructure. The project, financed by ADFD and implemented by Masdar, aims to strengthen electricity infrastructure, reduce the country’s heavy dependence on imported diesel, improve power reliability, and expand access to renewable energy. The facilities are expected to generate around 33.75 GWh of clean electricity annually, support energy and economic resilience, and reduce carbon emissions while contributing to the country’s transition toward a more sustainable energy system.
decision_making_institution: Abu Dhabi Fund for Development (ADFD)
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Released 400,000 common carp fingerlings into water bodies in Nineveh as part of the One Million Fingerlings Project. The initiative aims to increase fish stocks, support fishermen, develop the fisheries sector, promote sustainable agricultural and livestock activities, and strengthen national food security.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policy_description: Seed technology and quality assurance systems
policydecision_details: Two new seed purification and processing lines were inaugurated at the Ahlelah facility in Nineveh, increasing total processing capacity to 30 tonnes per hour. The expansion, implemented by the World Bank emergency loan project team in coordination with the Ministry of Agriculture, also includes 11 new storage units to increase wheat storage capacity. The initiative supports the development of Iraq’s seed sector, strengthens wheat storage and processing infrastructure, and enhances agricultural production capacity.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture
policycategory: Seed technology and quality assurance systems

policydecision_details: Implemented a national livestock vaccination campaign against major animal diseases, including brucellosis, foot-and-mouth disease, and PPR, through veterinary directorates and departments across several governorates. More than 4,600 livestock have been vaccinated against brucellosis, alongside additional vaccinations against foot-and-mouth disease and PPR, as veterinary teams continue reaching targeted herds and livestock breeders. The campaign aims to strengthen disease prevention and control, protect livestock health and production, support farmers’ livelihoods, and contribute to national food security.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Launched preparations for the 2026 olive harvest campaign in partnership with national and international institutions to support farmers, strengthen their resilience, and protect agricultural land. The campaign will coordinate field interventions, volunteers, and supporting organizations, with decentralized committees established in each town to organize harvesting activities and provide assistance to farmers in areas most in need. The initiative also aims to facilitate farmers’ access to their land and protect the olive harvest amid ongoing challenges and attacks against farmers and their property, while strengthening the resilience of the agricultural sector and its contribution to the national economy.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Supported agricultural marketing and strengthening the presence of local dates in regional markets. The seasonal market, organized and supervised by the Ministry’s Al-Mithnab office, brings together producers, marketers, and buyers through organized sales and auctions covering more than 70 date varieties. The Ministry also monitors incoming dates, ensures compliance with regulations and quality requirements, and provides an organized marketing environment that supports farmers, marketers, and consumers.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture

policydecision_details: Signed a cooperation agreement to launch a two-year Poultry Farm Biosecurity Programme aimed at strengthening disease prevention, surveillance, hygiene, and biosecurity practices at poultry farms. The programme will build the capacity of agricultural, livestock, animal health, and poultry-sector personnel, helping improve production efficiency, protect animal health, and strengthen food security in Abu Dhabi.
decision_making_institution: Abu Dhabi Agriculture and Food Safety Authority (ADAFSA)

policydecision_details: Launched an A-to-E Food Label Verification System to assess the accuracy of nutritional information displayed on packaged food products. The service tests whether declared levels of sugar, fat, calories, protein, carbohydrates, fibre, and sodium match the actual contents of products. The classification is intended to help food businesses validate nutritional claims, support regulatory compliance, and strengthen consumer confidence in food labelling. An A grade indicates accuracy of the nutritional information, not that the product is healthier.
decision_making_institution: Dubai Central Laboratory – Dubai Municipality

policydecision_details: Distributed two fodder seed production units to agricultural associations in Al-Burj and Surif to support more than 50 farmers directly and around 3,000 people indirectly. Funded by the European Union and the Palestinian government, the initiative provides agricultural machinery and seeds to reduce production costs, improve productivity, strengthen livestock production, and enhance the resilience and livelihoods of farming communities in Area C.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Developed an integrated logistics hub centred on Dakhla Atlantique, connecting the future port with the El Argoub logistics zone and the El Guerguerat trade corridor to strengthen trade links with Mauritania and sub-Saharan Africa. The USD 1.6 billion port, expected to begin operations in 2029, will have an annual capacity of 35 million tonnes and will be supported by a 1,650-hectare industrial zone. The integrated network is intended to improve logistics connectivity, facilitate trade, and position Dakhla as a regional gateway, although attracting shipping lines and maintaining competitive transport costs remain key challenges.
decision_making_institution: Government of Morocco

policydecision_details: Signed a memorandum of understanding with AMKM (UAE) and Aqua Bridge Holding to explore investment and development opportunities in the blue economy, aquaculture, sustainable fisheries, marine and freshwater resources, and food security. The cooperation covers developing fish hatcheries and farms, processing and cold-chain infrastructure, feasibility studies, advanced technologies, and international best practices to support sustainable use of water resources, economic development, and food security.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Developed a 200,000-ton grain storage silo project to establish a strategic reserve of essential commodities, including wheat, barley, corn, and soybeans, while increasing the port’s capacity to receive and handle grain shipments. The project includes 20 silos, grain-handling equipment, an electrical substation, and supporting facilities, and is expected to strengthen food supply security, improve grain logistics, and create 200–300 jobs once operational.
decision_making_institution: Julyana Free Zone

policy_description: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
policydecision_details: Launched an Integrated Digital Environmental Impact Assessment (IDEIA) system to streamline environmental approvals, reduce paperwork, and speed up investment procedures while maintaining environmental standards. The platform allows investors and consultants to submit and track environmental studies electronically, while enabling the Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA) to manage reviews and approvals through a central database. The initiative also supports Egypt’s green industrial transition, digital transformation, carbon compliance, and improved competitiveness of Egyptian industries and exports.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Environment, the Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade
policycategory: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources

policydecision_details: Signed agreements worth OMR1.19 million to restore and maintain 64 aflaj damaged by the recent low-pressure weather system in North Al Batinah. The programme covers 76 aflaj in total and aims to protect these vital water systems, supporting agricultural activity, local communities, and sustainable water management.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Water Resources

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Integrated its green hydrogen programme with a broader industrial ecosystem linking renewable energy, battery storage, green manufacturing, and exports. The approach aims to use solar and wind power with energy storage to provide reliable electricity for industries such as green ammonia, low-carbon fuels, iron and steel, while developing higher-value products for international markets. Hydrom is also focusing on stronger project frameworks, local capabilities, engineering capacity, and digital technologies to support commercially viable hydrogen and renewable energy projects.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Energy and Minerals
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Signed a memorandum of understanding with Al-Abbar Company, with the participation of the Agricultural Cooperative Bank, to provide farmers with agricultural machinery, equipment, and related tools through flexible installment plans. The initiative aims to modernize agricultural operations, improve production efficiency, reduce farmers’ financial burden, and promote the use of modern technologies to support sustainable agriculture and food security.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Signed an agreement with Relief American Fund to rehabilitate and develop the Al-Jalaa date palm farm in Al-Bukamal. The project will improve irrigation, pest and fertilizer management, and farm infrastructure, while introducing solar energy, expanding palm cultivation, and providing training and knowledge transfer. It also includes developing agricultural tourism facilities to increase the farm’s economic value and support the date palm sector in the area.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture

policydecision_details: Suspended foreign grape imports during the domestic harvest season to support local growers and improve the marketing of locally produced grapes. With production in Duhok expected to increase significantly, the measure is complemented by efforts to expand distribution to other Iraqi provinces and increase grape-processing capacity to manage surplus production and reduce post-harvest losses.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Agriculture and Water Resources

policydecision_details: Launched an AI-powered Smart Voice Assistant for its Nama e-services platform, allowing users to access government services through natural voice commands and receive tailored information on requirements and procedures. The initiative supports Saudi Arabia’s digital transformation by improving service accessibility, reducing the time and effort required to access services, and using data and AI to enhance service delivery and decision-making.
decision_making_institution: The Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture
